```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center")

library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# Resolve paths cleanly whether knitted from report/ or project root
out_dir <- if (dir.exists("outputs")) "outputs" else "../outputs"
plot_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "plots")

df         <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "clean.rds"))
dq_tbl     <- readr::read_csv(file.path(out_dir, "data_quality_summary.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
dropped_df <- readr::read_csv(file.path(out_dir, "dropped_columns.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
overall_r  <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "overall_results.rds"))
eda_r      <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "eda_results.rds"))
quest_r    <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "questions_results.rds"))
mining_r   <- readRDS(file.path(out_dir, "mining_results.rds"))

# Helper getters for inline stats (never hardcode any numbers)
n_total <- nrow(df)
get_num <- function(var, col) {
  overall_r$numeric_summary |>
    dplyr::filter(variable == var) |>
    dplyr::pull(!!rlang::sym(col))
}
get_prof <- function(var, cat) {
  overall_r$profile |>
    dplyr::filter(variable == var, category == cat)
}
get_flag <- function(pattern) {
  overall_r$flag_summary |>
    dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(flag, stringr::fixed(pattern)))
}
get_test <- function(comp_name) {
  eda_r$chisq_tests |>
    dplyr::filter(comparison == comp_name)
}
get_grp <- function(grp_name, val_name) {
  eda_r$group_averages |>
    dplyr::filter(grouping == grp_name, group_val == val_name)
}
get_out <- function(outlet_name, status_val) {
  eda_r$outlet_comparisons |>
    dplyr::filter(grouping == outlet_name, group_val == status_val)
}
get_imp <- function(lbl) {
  overall_r$improvements |>
    dplyr::filter(option_label == lbl)
}
get_q <- function(q_tbl, grp_val, item_lbl) {
  q_tbl |>
    dplyr::filter(as.character(group) == grp_val, item == item_lbl)
}
get_cor <- function(v1, v2) {
  eda_r$correlations |>
    dplyr::filter((var1 == v1 & var2 == v2) | (var1 == v2 & var2 == v1))
}
get_rule <- function(idx) {
  mining_r$rules_df |>
    dplyr::slice(idx)
}
get_tm <- function(m_name) {
  mining_r$tree_metrics |>
    dplyr::filter(metric == m_name) |>
    dplyr::pull(value)
}

# Derived summaries from clean.rds / outputs for inline text
nes_spend_tbl <- df |>
  dplyr::mutate(nes_user = dplyr::if_else(outlet_nescafe == 1, "User", "NonUser")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(spend_band, nes_user) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pct = round(100 * mean(satisfied), 1), .groups = "drop")
get_nes_band <- function(band_pat, who) {
  nes_spend_tbl |>
    dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(as.character(spend_band), stringr::fixed(band_pat)), nes_user == who) |>
    dplyr::pull(pct)
}

leaf_tbl <- df |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    leaf = dplyr::case_when(
      spend < 2250 ~ "low_spend",
      factor_hygiene_cleanliness == 1 ~ "high_hyg",
      TRUE ~ "high_nohyg"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(leaf) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    pct_sat = round(100 * mean(satisfied), 1),
    pct_unsat = round(100 * (1 - mean(satisfied)), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
get_leaf <- function(leaf_id) leaf_tbl |> dplyr::filter(leaf == leaf_id)
```

# Introduction

Understanding how university students eat on campus helps campus administrators, hostel mess committees, and food vendors improve food quality, hygiene, affordability, and outlet availability. In this **Campus Food Insights** project, we analyze a Google Form student survey covering campus outlet preferences, daily meals eaten at campus outlets, meal skipping, monthly extra spending, outside food ordering, overall satisfaction, decision factors, and wanted improvements.

The goal is simple and practical: clean the raw survey answers carefully, explore overall patterns and group differences using simple statistical checks (cross-tables, percentages, Pearson correlations, and chi-square tests), answer focused questions that emerge from the data, apply two data-mining techniques (**association rules** and a **decision tree**), and package everything into an interactive **Shiny dashboard** (`app/app.R`) and this final HTML report.

# Data Collection

The raw dataset (`data/dmaProjectdata.csv`) contains **`r n_total` student responses** across **`r dq_tbl$value[dq_tbl$metric == "Raw columns"]` columns**, collected via Google Forms on `10/11/2026` between `15:15:14` and `15:53:33` (a roughly 38-minute window).

Important sampling characteristics of who answered:

- **Year of study:** `r get_prof("year", "3rd Year")$count` students (`r get_prof("year", "3rd Year")$pct`%) are in **3rd Year**, `r get_prof("year", "1st Year")$count` (`r get_prof("year", "1st Year")$pct`%) in 1st Year, and `r get_prof("year", "2nd Year")$count` (`r get_prof("year", "2nd Year")$pct`%) in 2nd Year.
- **Residence:** `r get_prof("residence", "Hostel")$count` (`r get_prof("residence", "Hostel")$pct`%) live in the **Hostel**, and only `r get_prof("residence", "Day Scholar")$count` (`r get_prof("residence", "Day Scholar")$pct`%) are Day Scholars.
- **Gender:** `r get_prof("gender", "Male")$count` (`r get_prof("gender", "Male")$pct`%) are Male and `r get_prof("gender", "Female")$count` (`r get_prof("gender", "Female")$pct`%) are Female.
- **Rare groups (< 8 students):** Day Scholars (`r get_prof("residence", "Day Scholar")$count`), Vegans (`r get_prof("diet", "Vegan")$count`), and Cash payers (`r get_prof("payment", "Cash")$count`) each have fewer than 8 responses. Per project rules, we report **"too few responses"** rather than making subgroup claims for them.

# Cleaning

All cleaning steps live in `R/01_clean.R` and keep the raw CSV untouched. Key steps and quality checks:

1. **Duplicate check:** `r dq_tbl$value[dq_tbl$metric == "Exact duplicate rows (all cols)"]` exact duplicate rows and `r dq_tbl$value[dq_tbl$metric == "Duplicate rows (excluding Timestamp)"]` duplicate answer rows (excluding `Timestamp`).
2. **Empty columns dropped (`r nrow(dropped_df)` columns, 100% NA):** `Untitled Question`, all four dining facility-rating columns (*Infrastructure and Seating*, *Staff Friendliness*, *Operating Hours/Availability*, *Waste Management/Cleanliness*), and the *Nutrition Information* question were completely empty (`0 / 88` responses) and were dropped.
3. **Messy text-to-number fixes (`r dq_tbl$value[dq_tbl$metric == "Distinct rows with text-to-number fixes"]` distinct rows fixed, 0 NAs left):**
   - `meals_per_day` (`r dq_tbl$value[dq_tbl$metric == "Rows fixed in meals_per_day"]` rows): `"1-2 meals"` parsed to `1` (conservative lower bound via `readr::parse_number()`) and `"1 times"` parsed to `1`.
   - `spend` (`r dq_tbl$value[dq_tbl$metric == "Rows fixed in spend"]` rows): stripped `"Rs."` prefix and parsed `"Rs. 2,000/-"` to `2000` and `"around 1000"` to `1000`.
   - `outside_orders` (`r dq_tbl$value[dq_tbl$metric == "Rows fixed in outside_orders"]` rows): converted `"twice a week"` to `2` and parsed `"1 times"` to `1`.
4. **Multi-select splitting:** Split `outlets` (`9` options), `factors` (`11` options), and `improvements` (`11` options) into `31` binary `0/1` columns using `stringr::str_detect(..., fixed())`, with `0` count mismatches across all `88` rows.
5. **Derived helper columns & ordered factors:** Created ordered factors for `year` and `spend_band` (`Low (<= Rs 1,000)`, `Medium (Rs 1,001-2,000)`, `High (> Rs 2,000)`), plus binary flags:
   - `satisfied`: rating `>= 4` (`r get_flag("satisfied")$count` students, `r get_flag("satisfied")$pct`%).
   - `skips_breakfast`: skips Breakfast most often (`r get_flag("skips_breakfast")$count` students, `r get_flag("skips_breakfast")$pct`%).
   - `heavy_outside`: orders outside `>= 2` times/week (`r get_flag("heavy_outside")$count` students, `r get_flag("heavy_outside")$pct`%), separating the top fifth from the `r round(100 - get_flag("heavy_outside")$pct, 1)`% who order `0` or `1` time per week.

```{r tbl-dq}
knitr::kable(dq_tbl, caption = "Table 1: Data Quality and Cleaning Summary")
```

# Overall Analysis

Before exploring subgroups, we inspect the big-picture metrics across all `r n_total` respondents (`R/02_overall.R`):

- **Monthly extra food spend (excluding mess fees):** Mean = **Rs `r get_num("spend", "mean")`**, Median = **Rs `r get_num("spend", "median")`** (range Rs `r get_num("spend", "min")` to Rs `r get_num("spend", "max")`). Half of students (`r get_prof("spend_band", "Medium (Rs 1,001-2,000)")$pct`%, `r get_prof("spend_band", "Medium (Rs 1,001-2,000)")$count`) fall in the Medium band (`Rs 1,001-2,000`), `r get_prof("spend_band", "Low (<= Rs 1,000)")$pct`% (`r get_prof("spend_band", "Low (<= Rs 1,000)")$count`) spend `<= Rs 1,000`, and `r get_prof("spend_band", "High (> Rs 2,000)")$pct`% (`r get_prof("spend_band", "High (> Rs 2,000)")$count`) spend `> Rs 2,000`.
- **Meals & outside ordering:** Students eat an average of **`r get_num("meals_per_day", "mean")`** campus outlet meals/day (median `r get_num("meals_per_day", "median")`) and order outside food **`r get_num("outside_orders", "mean")`** times/week (median `r get_num("outside_orders", "median")`).
- **Diet & payment:** Vegetarian (`r get_prof("diet", "Vegetarian")$count`, `r get_prof("diet", "Vegetarian")$pct`%) and Non-Vegetarian (`r get_prof("diet", "Non-Vegetarian")$count`, `r get_prof("diet", "Non-Vegetarian")$pct`%) are equal in size, followed by Eggetarian (`r get_prof("diet", "Eggetarian")$count`, `r get_prof("diet", "Eggetarian")$pct`%) and Vegan (`r get_prof("diet", "Vegan")$count`, too few responses). UPI/QR Code accounts for **`r get_prof("payment", "UPI/QR Code")$pct`%** (`r get_prof("payment", "UPI/QR Code")$count` of `r n_total`).
- **Overall satisfaction:** Mean = **`r get_num("satisfaction", "mean")` / 5**, Median = **`r get_num("satisfaction", "median")`**. Nearly half (`r overall_r$satisfaction_dist$pct[3]`%, `r overall_r$satisfaction_dist$count[3]`) chose neutral `3`, `r sum(overall_r$satisfaction_dist$count[1:2])` (`r sum(overall_r$satisfaction_dist$pct[1:2])`%) are dissatisfied (`1` or `2`), and only **`r get_flag("satisfied")$count` (`r get_flag("satisfied")$pct`%)** are satisfied (`4` or `5`).
- **Meal skipping:** **`r get_prof("skipped_meal", "Breakfast")$pct`%** (`r get_prof("skipped_meal", "Breakfast")$count` of `r n_total`) skip **Breakfast** most often, far ahead of Lunch (`r get_prof("skipped_meal", "Lunch")$pct`%) and Evening Snack (`r get_prof("skipped_meal", "Evening Snack")$pct`%).

# EDA Facts

Using `R/03_eda.R`, we compared satisfaction, spend, breakfast skipping, and outside ordering across Year, Gender, Diet (excluding Vegan `n = 1`), Spend Band, and each outlet with at least 8 users (excluding Campus Café `n = 7`, Chai Vyanjan `n = 6`, Other Stalls `n = 5`, and Outside Delivery `n = 1`).

## Statistically Supported Facts (Chi-Square `p < 0.05`)

1. **Spend Band vs. Satisfaction (`p = `r get_test("Spend Band vs Satisfied")$p_value``):** High spenders (`> Rs 2,000`) are much more likely to be satisfied (`r get_grp("Spend Band", "High (> Rs 2,000)")$pct_satisfied`%, `r sum(df$spend_band == "High (> Rs 2,000)" & df$satisfied == 1)`/`r get_grp("Spend Band", "High (> Rs 2,000)")$n`) than Medium (`r get_grp("Spend Band", "Medium (Rs 1,001-2,000)")$pct_satisfied`%, `r sum(df$spend_band == "Medium (Rs 1,001-2,000)" & df$satisfied == 1)`/`r get_grp("Spend Band", "Medium (Rs 1,001-2,000)")$n`) and Low (`r get_grp("Spend Band", "Low (<= Rs 1,000)")$pct_satisfied`%, `r sum(df$spend_band == "Low (<= Rs 1,000)" & df$satisfied == 1)`/`r get_grp("Spend Band", "Low (<= Rs 1,000)")$n`) spenders.
2. **Nescafé Usage vs. Satisfaction (`p = `r get_test("Nescafé User vs Satisfied")$p_value``):** Nescafé users (`n = `r get_out("Nescafé", "Uses Outlet")$n``) are more than twice as likely to be satisfied (`r get_out("Nescafé", "Uses Outlet")$pct_satisfied`%, `r sum(df$outlet_nescafe == 1 & df$satisfied == 1)`/`r get_out("Nescafé", "Uses Outlet")$n`) as non-users (`r get_out("Nescafé", "Does Not Use")$pct_satisfied`%, `r sum(df$outlet_nescafe == 0 & df$satisfied == 1)`/`r get_out("Nescafé", "Does Not Use")$n`).
3. **Diet vs. Lower Prices Demand (`p = `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$p_value``):** Vegetarians ask for Lower Prices significantly more often (`r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$pct_yes`%, `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$count_yes`/`r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$n`) than Non-Vegetarians (`r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Non-Vegetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$pct_yes`%, `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Non-Vegetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$count_yes`/`r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Non-Vegetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$n`) and Eggetarians (`r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Eggetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$pct_yes`%, `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Eggetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$count_yes`/`r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Eggetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$n`).

## Noticeable Patterns Only (Not Confirmed at `p < 0.05` — May Be Luck)

- **Yadav Canteen & Breakfast Skipping (`p = `r get_test("Yadav Canteen User vs Skips Breakfast")$p_value``):** Yadav Canteen users skip breakfast less often (`r get_out("Yadav Canteen", "Uses Outlet")$pct_skips_breakfast`% vs `r get_out("Yadav Canteen", "Does Not Use")$pct_skips_breakfast`% for non-users).
- **Diet & Food Channels:** Vegetarians show higher heavy outside ordering (`r get_grp("Diet", "Vegetarian")$pct_heavy_outside`% vs `r get_grp("Diet", "Non-Vegetarian")$pct_heavy_outside`% Non-Veg, `p = `r get_test("Diet vs Heavy Outside Ordering")$p_value``), higher Hostel Mess use (`r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Uses Hostel Mess")$pct_yes`% vs `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Non-Vegetarian", "Uses Hostel Mess")$pct_yes`%, `p = `r get_test("Diet vs Uses Hostel Mess")$p_value``), and lower Night Canteen use (`r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Uses Night Canteen")$pct_yes`% vs `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Non-Vegetarian", "Uses Night Canteen")$pct_yes`%, `p = `r get_test("Diet vs Uses Night Canteen")$p_value``).
- **Night Canteen & Breakfast Skipping (`p = `r get_test("Night Canteen User vs Skips Breakfast")$p_value``):** `r get_out("Night Canteen", "Uses Outlet")$pct_skips_breakfast`% of Night Canteen users skip breakfast vs `r get_out("Night Canteen", "Does Not Use")$pct_skips_breakfast`% of non-users (not statistically supported).
- **Gender & Linear Correlations:** Male and Female students look nearly identical across all outcomes (`p >= `r min(eda_r$chisq_tests$p_value[eda_r$chisq_tests$x_var == "gender"])``), and all pairwise Pearson correlations between numeric columns are weak (`|r| <= `r max(abs(eda_r$correlations$r))``, all `p >= `r min(eda_r$correlations$p_value)``).

```{r fig-eda, out.width="88%"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, "07_eda_correlations_heatmap.png"))
```

# Questions and Answers

Five focused research questions were drawn directly from the strongest Phase 2 and Phase 3 findings (`R/04_questions.R`):

### Q1. Why are high spenders (> Rs 2,000/month) much more satisfied than low or medium spenders? {-}
High spenders (`n = `r quest_r$q1_numeric$n[1]``) eat fewer campus outlet meals per day (`r quest_r$q1_numeric$mean_meals_per_day[1]` vs `r quest_r$q1_numeric$mean_meals_per_day[2]`), order outside slightly more (`r quest_r$q1_numeric$mean_outside_orders[1]` vs `r quest_r$q1_numeric$mean_outside_orders[2]`/week; `r quest_r$q1_numeric$pct_heavy_outside[1]`% heavy vs `r quest_r$q1_numeric$pct_heavy_outside[2]`%), and use Nescafé more (`r get_q(quest_r$q1_comp, "High (> Rs 2,000)", "Uses Nescafé")$pct_yes`% vs `r get_q(quest_r$q1_comp, "Low/Med (<= Rs 2,000)", "Uses Nescafé")$pct_yes`%) while using Yadav Canteen less (`r get_q(quest_r$q1_comp, "High (> Rs 2,000)", "Uses Yadav Canteen")$pct_yes`% vs `r get_q(quest_r$q1_comp, "Low/Med (<= Rs 2,000)", "Uses Yadav Canteen")$pct_yes`%). None of those single item gaps reaches `p < 0.05` (`p = `r min(quest_r$q1_comp$p_value)`` to `r max(quest_r$q1_comp$p_value)`), and high spenders still ask for Better Quality (`r get_q(quest_r$q1_comp, "High (> Rs 2,000)", "Wants Better Food Quality")$pct_yes`%), Better Hygiene (`r get_q(quest_r$q1_comp, "High (> Rs 2,000)", "Wants Better Hygiene")$pct_yes`%), and Lower Prices (`r get_q(quest_r$q1_comp, "High (> Rs 2,000)", "Wants Lower Prices")$pct_yes`%). Higher budgets appear to buy flexibility rather than eliminating complaints, though the survey did not record *which* exact items high spenders buy.

```{r fig-q1, out.width="84%"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, "09_q1_high_spenders.png"))
```

### Q2. What sets Nescafé users apart from non-users, and does using Nescafé explain their higher satisfaction? {-}
Nescafé users (`n = `r quest_r$q2_numeric$n[1]``) pick more outlets overall (`r quest_r$q2_numeric$mean_outlets_picked[1]` vs `r quest_r$q2_numeric$mean_outlets_picked[2]`), spend slightly more (Rs `r quest_r$q2_numeric$mean_spend[1]` vs Rs `r quest_r$q2_numeric$mean_spend[2]`), and show higher satisfaction within **every** spend band (`r get_nes_band("Low", "User")`% vs `r get_nes_band("Low", "NonUser")`% in Low, `r get_nes_band("Medium", "User")`% vs `r get_nes_band("Medium", "NonUser")`% in Medium, and `r get_nes_band("High", "User")`% vs `r get_nes_band("High", "NonUser")`% in High). Still, their improvement requests match non-users (`r get_q(quest_r$q2_comp, "Nescafé User", "Wants Better Hygiene")$pct_yes`% Hygiene, `r get_q(quest_r$q2_comp, "Nescafé User", "Wants Better Quality")$pct_yes`% Quality, `r get_q(quest_r$q2_comp, "Nescafé User", "Wants Lower Prices")$pct_yes`% Lower Prices). Because the survey measured only overall campus satisfaction rather than per-outlet ratings, we cannot prove Nescafé directly caused the higher rating.

### Q3. Who skips breakfast most often, and how is skipping breakfast linked to outlet choices? {-}
Breakfast skipping (`r get_flag("skips_breakfast")$pct`%) cuts evenly across Year, Gender, and Diet (`p >= `r min(get_test("Year vs Skips Breakfast")$p_value, get_test("Gender vs Skips Breakfast")$p_value, get_test("Diet vs Skips Breakfast")$p_value)``). The main contrast is outlet choice: only `r get_q(quest_r$q3_comp, "Skips Breakfast (n=62)", "Uses Yadav Canteen")$pct_yes`% of breakfast skippers use Yadav Canteen vs `r get_q(quest_r$q3_comp, "Skips Other/Rarely (n=26)", "Uses Yadav Canteen")$pct_yes`% of non-skippers (`p = `r get_q(quest_r$q3_comp, "Skips Breakfast (n=62)", "Uses Yadav Canteen")$p_value``), while Night Canteen leans higher among skippers (`r get_q(quest_r$q3_comp, "Skips Breakfast (n=62)", "Uses Night Canteen")$pct_yes`% vs `r get_q(quest_r$q3_comp, "Skips Other/Rarely (n=26)", "Uses Night Canteen")$pct_yes`%, `p = `r get_q(quest_r$q3_comp, "Skips Breakfast (n=62)", "Uses Night Canteen")$p_value``), and skippers are twice as likely to eat `0` campus outlet meals per day (`r quest_r$q3_numeric$pct_zero_campus_meals[1]`% vs `r quest_r$q3_numeric$pct_zero_campus_meals[2]`%). Sleep hours and class schedules were not collected, so the root cause cannot be verified.

```{r fig-q3, out.width="82%"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, "11_q3_breakfast_skipping.png"))
```

### Q4. Do Vegetarian and Non-Vegetarian students rely on different food channels or want different improvements? {-}
Vegetarians (`n = `r get_grp("Diet", "Vegetarian")$n``) use Hostel Mess more (`r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Uses Hostel Mess")$pct_yes`% vs `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Non-Vegetarian", "Uses Hostel Mess")$pct_yes`%, `p = `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Uses Hostel Mess")$p_value``), Night Canteen less (`r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Uses Night Canteen")$pct_yes`% vs `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Non-Vegetarian", "Uses Night Canteen")$pct_yes`%, `p = `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Uses Night Canteen")$p_value``), and order outside `>= 2` times/week three times as often (`r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Heavy Outside Orders (>=2/wk)")$pct_yes`% vs `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Non-Vegetarian", "Heavy Outside Orders (>=2/wk)")$pct_yes`%, `p = `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Heavy Outside Orders (>=2/wk)")$p_value``), while requesting **Lower Prices** significantly more often (`r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$pct_yes`% vs `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Non-Vegetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$pct_yes`% Non-Veg, `p = `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$p_value``). Overall satisfaction does not differ reliably (`p = `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Satisfied (4-5)")$p_value``), and Vegans (`n = `r get_prof("diet", "Vegan")$count``) have too few responses.

```{r fig-q4, out.width="84%"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, "12_q4_diet_channels.png"))
```

### Q5. Do dissatisfied students ask for different improvements than neutral or satisfied students? {-}
No—improvement demands are campus-wide. Across Dissatisfied (`1-2`, `n = `r sum(df$satisfaction <= 2)``), Neutral (`3`, `n = `r sum(df$satisfaction == 3)``), and Satisfied (`4-5`, `n = `r sum(df$satisfaction >= 4)``) students, nearly half in every tier ask for Better Hygiene (`r get_q(quest_r$q5_comp, "Dissatisfied (1-2)", "Better Hygiene/Cleanliness")$pct_yes`%, `r get_q(quest_r$q5_comp, "Neutral (3)", "Better Hygiene/Cleanliness")$pct_yes`%, `r get_q(quest_r$q5_comp, "Satisfied (4-5)", "Better Hygiene/Cleanliness")$pct_yes`%; `p = `r get_q(quest_r$q5_comp, "Dissatisfied (1-2)", "Better Hygiene/Cleanliness")$p_value``), Better Food Quality (`r get_q(quest_r$q5_comp, "Dissatisfied (1-2)", "Better Food Quality")$pct_yes`%, `r get_q(quest_r$q5_comp, "Neutral (3)", "Better Food Quality")$pct_yes`%, `r get_q(quest_r$q5_comp, "Satisfied (4-5)", "Better Food Quality")$pct_yes`%; `p = `r get_q(quest_r$q5_comp, "Dissatisfied (1-2)", "Better Food Quality")$p_value``), and Lower Prices (`r get_q(quest_r$q5_comp, "Dissatisfied (1-2)", "Lower Prices")$pct_yes`%, `r get_q(quest_r$q5_comp, "Neutral (3)", "Lower Prices")$pct_yes`%, `r get_q(quest_r$q5_comp, "Satisfied (4-5)", "Lower Prices")$pct_yes`%; `p = `r get_q(quest_r$q5_comp, "Dissatisfied (1-2)", "Lower Prices")$p_value``). Because the four facility-rating columns were completely empty, the survey cannot tell which specific physical facility aspect drove low satisfaction.

# Data Mining Results

## Association Rules (`arules / apriori`)

Using `support >= 0.14` (`>= 13` students), `confidence >= 0.65`, and `lift > 1.15`, we found **`r nrow(mining_r$rules_df)` non-redundant rules**. Top rules highlight clear patterns of complaints and habits:

- `` `r get_rule(1)$rules` `` (`count = `r get_rule(1)$count``, `conf = `r get_rule(1)$confidence``, `lift = `r get_rule(1)$lift``)
- `` `r get_rule(3)$rules` `` (`count = `r get_rule(3)$count``, `conf = `r get_rule(3)$confidence``, `lift = `r get_rule(3)$lift``)
- `` `r get_rule(5)$rules` `` (`count = `r get_rule(5)$count``, `conf = `r get_rule(5)$confidence``, `lift = `r get_rule(5)$lift``)
- `` `r get_rule(14)$rules` `` (`count = `r get_rule(14)$count``, `conf = `r get_rule(14)$confidence``, `lift = `r get_rule(14)$lift``)

```{r tbl-rules}

```

## Decision Tree (`rpart`)

Predicting `satisfied` (`rating >= 4`), the majority-class baseline (`Not_Satisfied`) is **`r get_tm("Baseline accuracy (%)")`%**. With 10-fold cross-validation (`cp = `r get_tm("Best CV cp")``), CV accuracy is **`r get_tm("10-fold CV accuracy - pruned (%)")`%** (in-sample accuracy = `r get_tm("In-sample accuracy of plotted tree (%)")`%).

In plain language: first, the tree splits at monthly spend `< Rs 2,250`, where `r get_leaf("low_spend")$pct_unsat`% of the `r get_leaf("low_spend")$n` lower/medium spenders are not satisfied. Among the `r get_leaf("high_hyg")$n + get_leaf("high_nohyg")$n` students spending `>= Rs 2,250`, satisfaction splits on whether Hygiene/Cleanliness is a top decision factor: high spenders who prioritize Hygiene (`n = `r get_leaf("high_hyg")$n``) are still `r get_leaf("high_hyg")$pct_unsat`% unsatisfied, whereas high spenders who do not flag Hygiene (`n = `r get_leaf("high_nohyg")$n``) are `r get_leaf("high_nohyg")$pct_sat`% satisfied.

# Dashboard Description

The interactive dashboard (`app/app.R`) loads precomputed results from `outputs/` for fast startup and provides **Year, Diet, and Gender** sidebar filters that apply across all seven tabs:

1. **Overview:** Live `n = X` KPI cards and `plotly` bars for satisfaction, outlets, factors, and improvements.
2. **EDA Facts:** Interactive group comparison selector (flagging groups `< 8` in grey), live correlation heatmap, and searchable chi-square test table.
3. **Questions & Answers:** Dropdown for Q1–Q5 with triggering facts, plain-language summaries, and live filtered `plotly` charts.
4. **Association Rules:** Interactive Lift vs. Confidence bubble chart and `DT` table showing live match counts inside the active filter.
5. **Decision Tree:** `rpart.plot` visual, live leaf satisfaction bars, and baseline vs. CV accuracy summary.
6. **Recommendations:** Actionable takeaways for administration, vendors, and students alongside live filtered priority percentages.
7. **Data:** Searchable `DT` table of filtered records with one-click CSV download.

Every view prints `n = X` and displays an automatic warning banner whenever fewer than `10` students remain.

# Recommendations

1. **Prioritize campus-wide hygiene audits (Administration):** Better Hygiene/Cleanliness (`r get_imp("Better Hygiene/Cleanliness")$pct`%) is the #1 requested improvement across every satisfaction level and is the exact split holding back satisfaction even among high spenders.
2. **Improve Hostel Mess taste and quality (Administration & Mess Committee):** Better Food Quality (`r get_imp("Better Food Quality")$pct`%) is the #2 improvement overall, and association rules tie Hostel Mess directly to Better Taste (`conf = `r get_rule(5)$confidence``, `lift = `r get_rule(5)$lift``).
3. **Introduce quick, affordable breakfast options (Vendors & Administration):** `r get_flag("skips_breakfast")$pct`% skip breakfast most often (`r get_out("Night Canteen", "Uses Outlet")$pct_skips_breakfast`% among Night Canteen users), whereas Yadav Canteen users skip far less (`r get_out("Yadav Canteen", "Uses Outlet")$pct_skips_breakfast`%). Grab-and-go morning combos near hostels could recover missed meals.
4. **Offer affordable vegetarian & Nescafé value combos (Vendors):** Vegetarians request Lower Prices significantly more often (`r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$pct_yes`% vs `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Non-Vegetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$pct_yes`% Non-Veg, `p = `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$p_value``) and order outside heavily (`r get_grp("Diet", "Vegetarian")$pct_heavy_outside`%), while Nescafé users pair Better Quality + Lower Prices (`lift = `r get_rule(1)$lift``).
5. **Fix form validation for future surveys (Administration):** Make the dining-facility rating matrix and nutrition question required or properly linked in the next Google Form wave so facility-level scores are captured.

# Limitations

- **Small sample size (`n = `r n_total``):** Reduces statistical power for detecting modest differences and leaves Day Scholars (`r get_prof("residence", "Day Scholar")$count`), Vegans (`r get_prof("diet", "Vegan")$count`), Cash payers (`r get_prof("payment", "Cash")$count`), and four smaller outlets (`<= 7` users) with too few responses for valid subgroup claims.
- **Biased sample composition:** `r get_prof("year", "3rd Year")$pct`% of respondents are 3rd-year students, `r get_prof("residence", "Hostel")$pct`% live in hostels, and `r get_prof("gender", "Male")$pct`% are male—all collected within a single 38-minute burst—so findings mostly describe 3rd-year hostel residents.
- **Self-reported estimates:** Monthly spending (Rs `r get_num("spend", "min")`–`r get_num("spend", "max")`), meals per day, and weekly outside orders rely on student recall and rough text entries (e.g., `"1-2 meals"`, `"around 1000"`).
- **Empty facility-rating and nutrition columns:** All four dining facility ratings (Infrastructure/Seating, Staff Friendliness, Operating Hours, Waste Management/Cleanliness) and the nutrition question had `0 / `r n_total`` non-missing answers and had to be excluded.

# Conclusion

Across `r n_total` surveyed students, overall campus food satisfaction is lukewarm (mean = `r get_num("satisfaction", "mean")` / 5, only `r get_flag("satisfied")$pct`% satisfied), `r get_flag("skips_breakfast")$pct`% skip breakfast most often, and UPI/QR Code payments are nearly universal (`r get_prof("payment", "UPI/QR Code")$pct`%). Statistical tests and data mining reinforce a consistent story: students with larger monthly budgets (`> Rs 2,000`) and Nescafé users report higher satisfaction, yet demands for **Better Hygiene (`r get_imp("Better Hygiene/Cleanliness")$pct`%)**, **Better Food Quality (`r get_imp("Better Food Quality")$pct`%)**, and **Lower Prices (`r get_imp("Lower Prices")$pct`% — especially `r get_q(quest_r$q4_comp, "Vegetarian", "Wants Lower Prices")$pct_yes`% among Vegetarians)** span the entire campus. Focusing first on hygiene enforcement, mess food quality, vegetarian affordability, and quick breakfast availability directly addresses the biggest evidence-backed gaps.
